The registered PDF is arXiv:2201.05149v2, stamped 1 February 2024, by Hamed Hassani and Adel Javanmard. The title, 86-page length and SHA-256 agree with the original pinned audit. No source-version substitution was made.

Independent main-text enumeration finds exactly Theorem 4.2 on page 11 and Theorem 6.9 on page 20. Both complete statements were visually compared with fresh PDF renders. Theorem 6.9 is retained despite appearing in the proof-outline section; nearby Propositions, Lemmas and the quoted external theorem on page 21 are not counted. Main discussion ends on page 22 before acknowledgments, funding and the supplement notice; references continue through page 25. The supplement starts on page 26 and is excluded.

Theorem 4.2 retains its scalar sigma-squared definition, all five saddle variables, nonnegative optimization domains, complete objective, indicator threshold, nested lambda supremum, unique-root equation, and adversarial-risk limit. Training epsilon and test epsilon_test remain distinct. The probability statement explicitly includes both the training data and random weights. Superscript nu-star in the root and subscript nu_star in the final formula are preserved rather than silently equated.

Theorem 6.9 retains both full penalized objectives, positive lambda/lambda_s/lambda_w, the assumed weight event and the iff statement about convergence of optimum values. Phi_A contains an absolute residual, while Phi_B lacks those bars in the printed theorem. The adjacent Proposition 6.10 has a different noisy-linear objective with bars; it is not substituted into the theorem.

All twelve source passages were checked. The Gaussian linear data model, sphere-distributed random features fixed during coefficient fitting, shifted ReLU, adversarial risk, robust empirical objective and explicit Stieltjes-transform formula are preserved. The source gives Gaussian noise marginals but does not explicitly state independence of noise and covariates in (2.1); no independence clause was inserted. The source-defined transform formula is available in the main text, so its appendix reference was not followed.

The weight event retains its operator-norm bound and pairwise row inner-product bound. The matrix J retains both its fixed-W expectation definition and the explicit Hadamard/arccos formula on page 17. The expectation is over a Gaussian covariate; the matrix under its square root is positive semidefinite. Only the defining fragment of eta from Proposition 6.4 is used, without its concentration theorem or coefficient constraint set.

The activation decomposition retains mu0=0, mu1=1/2 and mu2=sqrt(1/4-1/(2 pi)), its Gaussian moment definitions and orthogonality conditions. The noisy features use the same W and a Gaussian u explicitly independent of x. The subsequent sample statement is read conditional on the shared W. The printed claim that sigma(Wx) has unit variance is archived as a discrepancy; it does not change the shifted activation into a standardized one.

All eleven auxiliary passages, source names, naming contexts and highlight selectors were checked. The asymptotic dimensional convention repeated in Section 6 is separate from Assumption 1’s signal normalization. Theorem 6.9 does not explicitly cite the latter normalization. All-ones-vector and matrix-norm notation are resolved without importing the surrounding auxiliary penalized loss.

All fourteen direct uses and fifteen related-theorem connections were reviewed. Theorem 4.2 uses D1-D7; it does not acquire the proof-only J matrix, Gaussian surrogate, weight event or auxiliary regularization. Theorem 6.9 uses its own explicitly referenced objects and the proportional-growth convention; the activation decomposition D10 is its sole indirect-only dependency. Nearby propositions are not promoted to theorem prerequisites.

The saved source notes preserve zero-boundary divisions in the scalar saddle objective, unspecified root domain, missing root evaluation identification, separate scalar/vector uses of beta and sigma, incomplete joint-randomness clauses, and unspecified penalty/limit regimes. The arbitrary-model risk definition does not supply general maximum-attainment conditions, and the ERM gives no tie-selection rule. These issues remain source limitations rather than silent repairs or proof certification.

The census content and original audit artifacts remain unchanged. Earlier scripts were archived under review-history/before-local-source-rebuild/scripts. The inventory writer now verifies the fixed registered PDF; content writers use main entry points, and scripts/rebuild.py regenerates all six JSON content artifacts in an empty directory. The reproduction check confirms byte-for-byte identity, and separate validator processes accept the inventory and final census.
